Theme

Body, health & movement · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

weakness noun

also weak (feeble), feebleness, frailty, infirmity, a weak point

classical

Cic. Att. 11.6.4 (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BC 2.15.2: māteriae, of timber (Lewis & Short)

imbēcillitās, imbēcillitātis f.

noun, third declension

weakness, feebleness

Of the body, of health, and of anything that lacks strength, and so helplessness; weak is imbēcillus (Cic. Amic. 23: imbēcillī valent, the weak are strong). A weak point in a person or an argument is a vitium.

Other words

  • īnfirmitās, īnfirmitātis f. — lack of strength, weakness; in later Latin, illness

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 33; Cic. Fam. 7.1: summa gracilitās et īnfirmitās corporis (Lewis & Short)

    Of children, of the body, of a building; from Pliny and Suetonius on also sickness, indisposition (Lewis & Short). Weak is īnfirmus.

Examples

  • Tulliae meae morbus et imbēcillitās corporis mē exanimat

    my Tullia’s illness and physical weakness are killing me with worryCic. Att. 11.6.4 (Lewis & Short)

  • ut et īnfirmitās puerōrum et ferōcitās juvenum et gravitās jam cōnstantis aetātis et senectūtis mātūritās nātūrāle quiddam habeat, quod suō tempore percipī dēbeat

    so that the weakness of children, the fire of the young, the gravity of settled middle age and the ripeness of old age each have something natural about them, to be gathered in its own seasonCic. Sen. 33

See also disease.
